doc.title: Denny Zeitlin interviewed by Monk Rowe, San Francisco, California, August 8, 2002

title: Musical geniuses and his record collection
summary: He names Parker, Powell, Miles, Coltrane, Russell, Coleman and Shorter as innovators, and describes his broad listening.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young

blocks.x: Wow. Well said. I had a question and you just made me forget it. That was so interesting what you were saying. Do you have people that, in your opinion, would be considered to be musical geniuses? I think that personally speaking the word genius is bandied about an awful lot. And I’m wondering, in the people that you enjoy listening to over the years, have there been a couple that you would consider to be geniuses?

I agree with you that the word is so highly charged and it would be so difficult to define. I mean I do think, when I think of the real incredible innovators and trailblazers in our music I tend to think of people like Charlie Parker, Bud Powell, Miles Davis, John Coltrane, George Russell, Ornette Coleman, people like that. I think — Wayne Shorter is another huge giant in my view in terms of a kind of unique contribution to the music over a long period of time. I’m sure I’m leaving out people that I love. Because there’s so many people that I admire. But those are some people that at least at this moment leaped into the foreground when I think of major, major people.
Okay. If I was to look — I’m assuming maybe you have a shelf of CDs or LPs.
So many I couldn’t begin to catalogue them.
Who would I find a lot of there? Who would I find?

Oh you’d find all those people I mentioned plus hosts of other players. I mean I feel I’ve been able to learn and get something from listening to virtually everybody I’ve ever purchased a CD or LP of. And I have quite a voracious appetite for just a wide range of music, unusual ethnic music too, classical music ranging from Bach all the way to the most modern atonal kinds of things, and some rock & roll I like a lot and funk bands and electronic music. So there’s an awful lot of music I love a lot.
